chunks: The holder of authority is like the rider on a lion — he is envied for his position, but he well knows his position.

key_terms.صَاحِبُ السُّلْطَانِ: The holder of authority or ruler
key_terms.يُغْبَطُ: Is envied or congratulated for a position

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the ruler being like a lion rider in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this metaphor from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) illustrates the dual nature of political authority: it is outwardly envied for its prestige but inwardly burdensome, requiring the ruler to possess deep, solitary insight into the volatile 'lion' of power. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that true leadership demands not just external control but internal spiritual and intellectual vigilance to prevent being devoured by the responsibilities and temptations of rule. The comparison underscores the isolation of the leader who must constantly manage the beast of statecraft while others merely admire the spectacle.
